reasons: A small tool with three subcommands is well within what argparse subparsers handle cleanly.
The standard library adds no dependency, so nothing to install, pin or upgrade over years of single-person maintenance.
argparse has been stable for a very long time, so there is little risk of breaking changes or abandonment.
click and typer would add a third-party dependency (typer also pulls in click) for little benefit at this size.

evidence.claim: I did not inspect the repo. This rests on general knowledge that argparse supports subcommands through add_subparsers and ships with Python 3.11.
evidence.source: Python standard library documentation (not fetched in this session)

risks: I did not check whether the repo already uses click or typer elsewhere. If it does, matching that would be better for consistency.
If the CLI grows to many nested subcommands or needs rich completion, argparse gets verbose and a switch would be worth it.
argparse needs more boilerplate than typer for typed arguments.
would_change_if: The repo already standardizes on click or typer, or the tool is expected to grow well past three subcommands with complex options.
